Seminar Title:

Neuromorphic IC Design Using Spiking Neural Network for Arrhythmia Classification

Seminar Type:

Speaker Name:

Samanway Ghosh ( Rollno : 524ec1008)

Speaker Type:

Date and Time:

01 Oct 2026 10:00

Contact:

Atin Mukherjee

Abstract:

Early detection of cardiac arrhythmias is critical for timely intervention to reduce mortality. Continuous and prolonged ECG monitoring using wearable devices are essential for early medical interventions. Due to prolonged use, it is prudent to build low power wearable devices with advanced AI algorithms for accurate arrhythmia classification to reduce mortality. Despite producing accuracy greater than 99%, traditional deep neural networks, such as &ndash RNNs, CNNs, transformer neural networks are often unsuitable for wearable devices due to their high computational and power requirements. Spiking neural networks (SNN) show low power consumption due to their event-based sparse computation &ndash mimicking the biological neurons. This work proposes a SNN model for arrhythmia detection with high accuracy and low-power hardware implementation. The proposed model employs de-noising, segmentation, and rate coding to preprocess the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database signals, which are then classified using a SNN, trained with STBP algorithm. A multiplier-less design with conditional accumulation and shift-based leakage scaling is implemented for hardware efficiency. The proposed model achieves 98.75% accuracy and 98.67% F1 score, outperforming existing SNN-based models. The FPGA implementation on a ZCU104 achieves functional equivalence with the software model, while consuming only 12 mW of dynamic power and attaining a latency of 417.82 ms/beat, thus demonstrating suitability for low-power, real-time wearable devices.
